If the problem is that the inner connections have expanded, I would say a quick option/test would be to just add a solder layer to the headphone jack itself. Take an old set of headphones and heat the 3 main contact rings [could start with the one right above the very tip - that one might be good enough to hold everything in] and solder a smooth layer of solder on.

The added solder would increase the thickness of the rings and act like a tape - but would be bonded to the metal, meaning no hassle with tape or other things.

The tip probably doesn't need to be soldered because that connector is spring loaded to slide over the angled portion. But if all of the inner connections have been affected, then the tip might need to be soldered too.

Obligatory cautions: Don't bridge any of the ring connectors, or the headphones won't work.

Practice soldering on a useless set first because the plastic ring insulators may melt at high heat loads.

It may be possible to get away with a single solder bulge on a single ring to hold it in place - a quick tack-weld approach would reduce the heat load on the plastic and minimize the risk of shorting any of the rings together.
